reasoning: Both attempts build a solid shared reactive screen-state module, one global UIScale, layout switching driven by PreferredInput and screen size, and touch placement clear of the thumbstick and jump button. A misses criterion 6: the title's UITextSizeConstraint stays at 24 real pixels, so the title stays small on 4K, the exact problem the user reported. B fixes the text with a fixed TextSize, but has a luau-lsp type error in its own code (a derived layout widened to string). That is a real check failure but a one-line annotation fix with no runtime effect, while A's flaw is a visible bug on the user's main complaint. B wins narrowly.

criteria.note: Responsive.luau holds input as a module-level source fed by PreferredInput changes; Screen.luau derives Size/Scale/SizeClass from `changed("AbsoluteSize")` (CoreUISafeInsets accounts for the topbar inset) and passes them down through Vide context, all reactive.
One UIScale on a Root frame sized 1/scale under each Screen, with scale = shortSide/1020 clamped 1..3 in Responsive.computeScale.

criteria.criterion: 3. Small screens change layout, not shrink
criteria.note: Scale never drops below 1; Compact/touch switches to the horizontal Bar layout with TOUCH_TILE_SIZE = 48.
toInputKind maps UserInputService.PreferredInput; isBar = isTouch or Compact or the column doesn't fit.
The Bar sits at top centre (UDim2.new(0.5,0,0,Margin)) inside a CoreUISafeInsets ScreenGui, so it avoids both bottom corners and the topbar.

criteria.criterion: 6. Title text keeps up with scale
criteria.note: The title keeps TextScaled with UITextSizeConstraint MaxTextSize = 24, and that real-pixel cap is not multiplied by Scale, so the title stays capped at 24 px on 4K.
Valid Vide (derive for metrics, context wraps Content), selection still works, and luau-lsp, selene and StyLua all pass.
Screen.luau holds module-level sources for the viewport (following CurrentCamera replacement), the topbar inset, PreferredInput and ViewportDisplaySize, refreshed in a batch on each change signal.
ScaledScreenGui puts one UIScale bound to Screen.uiScale (shortSide/1080 clamped 1..3) under the ScreenGui.

criteria.criterion: 3. Small screens change layout, not shrink
criteria.note: Minimum scale is 1; phone-sized screens get the CompactRow layout with 48 px tiles and 14 px names.
pickerLayout uses Screen.isPhone (viewport size) and Screen.isTouch (PreferredInput == Touch).
Row layouts are anchored top-right at a 12 px margin inside a CoreUISafeInsets ScreenGui, away from the thumbstick and above the jump button.

criteria.criterion: 6. Title text keeps up with scale
criteria.note: The title switches to a fixed TextSize = 22 and drops UITextSizeConstraint, so the UIScale grows it.
Runtime logic is sound Vide, but luau-lsp reports a TypeError in its own Main.client.luau: the `derive(pickerLayout)` result is inferred as `string` rather than the Layout type.

strengths: Clean context-based Screen + Responsive design that later screens can reuse, plus README docs
Screen size measured from the ScreenGui's AbsoluteSize with safe insets, so the topbar and notches are already excluded
Touch-friendly top-centre bar with 48 px tiles; number-key hints for keyboard players
weaknesses: Title's MaxTextSize cap isn't scaled, so the title stays small on 4K, which is the user's complaint
Non-touch Compact bar still uses 40 px tiles

strengths: Thorough shared Screen module (viewport, inset, input, large-display boost, Simulate hook for stories)
Three distinct layouts, including a thumb-sized Row for tablets and CompactRow for phones
ScaledScreenGui wrapper is easy for the next screens to reuse
weaknesses: luau-lsp type error in its own Main.client.luau
Placement logic lives in Main rather than in a reusable layout helper
Topbar inset is tracked but only fed to usableSize, which nothing uses
